Spencer Knight made 28 saves for the Blackhawks, who lost for the first time in three games with star Connor Bedard back in the lineup from shoulder surgery. Bedard, who recorded three points in his first two games of the season, was held to two shots on goal Saturday. Dallas appeared to open the scoring with 7:50 remaining in the first period, but Robertson's goal was overturned upon a Chicago video review challenge for offside. However, Robertson was rewarded with the game's first goal at 4:58 into the second period, when he converted a give-and-go with Mikko Rantanen. The Stars made it 2-0 with 5:50 remaining in the middle frame. After Oettinger made an elbow save on a Chicago redirect, Dallas transitioned into a two-on-one where Sam Steel fed Hyry, who beat Knight on the rush. Then, amid a line change just 1:27 into the third period, Hyry took a stretch pass from Nils Lundkvist, broke in and sent a backhander past Knight. Dallas added more insurance with 10:20 remaining, when Hintz sent in a successful wrister from the circle through some traffic that appeared to screen Knight. --Field Level Media

item.title: Islanders get first road win of season as Leafs lose again
item.description: The New York Islanders secured their first road win of the season with a 4-1 victory over the Toronto Maple Leafs on Saturday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The New York Islanders secured their first road win of the season with a 4-1 victory over the Toronto Maple Leafs on Saturday night. Anthony Duclair and Bo Horvat put the Islanders up 2-0 after 40 minutes and Simon Holmstrom secured the win with a pair of goals in the game's final six minutes as New York improved to 1-2-1 away from home. Horvat added an assist on Holmstrom's first goal and Ilya Sorokin continued his hot start, turning away 28 shots in his fourth win of the season. Sergei Bobrovsky stopped 16 of 19 shots for Toronto, which got a goal from Colton Sissons. Duclair opened the scoring 8:18 into the game. Jean-Gabriel Pageau pursued Toronto's Kirill Marchenko behind the net, recovered possession along the sideboards and fed Duclair in the slot, who placed his shot under the arm of Bobrovsky for his second of the year. Bobrovsky slid across the crease to deny Kyle Palmieri with a minute and a half left in the second, but Horvat chipped in the rebound between Bobrovsky and a sprawling Troy Stecher to make it 2-0. Both teams combined for just 12 shots in the middle frame. Sissons brought Toronto within a goal 3:54 into the third period, tipping in Stecher's low one-timer from the point. Both of Sissons' goals on the season have come against the Islanders. Little more than 10 minutes later, Horvat fed the puck to Holmstrom, who ripped the puck past Bobrovsky from the slot and halted a late offensive surge from the home team. Holmstrom followed up with an empty netter with just over two minutes remaining. With John Tavares out week-to-week (lower-body injury), Nick Paul slotted in at center on the Maple Leafs' second line. Islanders forwards Matias Maccelli and Calum Ritchie both left the game with injuries in the first period. New York's forward corps may be stretched even thinner in the ongoing absence of Mathew Barzal. Toronto has allowed three goals or more in seven consecutive games and has lost three straight. --Field Level Media

item.title: サッカー＝チェルシーＧＫマルティネス、脳震とうで病院に搬送
item.description: ［リバプール １７日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［リバプール　１７日　ロイター］ - サッカーのイングランド・プレミアリーグ、チェルシーのＧＫエミリアノ・マルティネス（３４）は１７日、エバートン戦で相手選手と衝突して脳震とうを起こし、病院に搬送された。

マルティネスはゴール前でＦＫに対応しようとした際、エバートンのジャラッド・ブランスウェイトと激突。ブランスウェイトは治療を受けた後に立ち上がったが、マルティネスは地面に横たわったまま治療を受けたのち、担架でピッチから運び出された。

チェルシーのシャビアロンソ監督は「脳震とうということ以外は分からない」とした上で、「彼は搬送されたとき意識はあり、今は病院で念のため検査を受けている。重傷ではないことを願っているが、待つしかない」と述べた。

後半３０分からマルティネスに代わり、２１歳のＧＫマイク・ペンダースが出場。プレミアリーグデビューを果たし、チームにとってリーグ戦では１月以来となる完封に貢献した。チェルシーはペドロ・ネトが２ゴールを挙げ、２─０で勝利した。

item.title: Argentinos Juniors gana a Banfield y trepa a cima de tabla anual del fútbol argentino
item.description: Argentinos Juniors venció el sábado 1-0 en su visita a Banfield y quedó en la cima de la tabla anual del fútbol argentino junto con Boca Juniors a falta de tres jornadas para el final.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Argentinos Juniors venció el sábado 1-0 en su visita a Banfield y quedó en la cima de la tabla anual del fútbol argentino junto con Boca Juniors a falta de tres jornadas para el final. Argentinos llegó a 54 puntos en la sumatoria general, misma cantidad de Boca, en busca de uno de los títulos de la temporada del fútbol argentino. Ambos aprovecharon el empate de Independiente Rivadavia, que quedó escolta con 53 unidades. En el partido disputado en el estadio Florencio Sola de Banfield, el gol del triunfo lo anotó el ingresado Matías Giménez Rojas a los 66 minutos tras una gran jugada individual. "Una felicidad enorme porque todo el año venimos peleándola y este es el resultado. Nos quedan tres finales. Hay que salir campeón, porque hace dos o tres años Argentinos viene llegando lejos hasta el final y no puede coronar, ojalá podamos ahora", dijo Giménez Rojas a la televisión local. Por su parte, en el estadio Bautista Gargantini de la provincia de Mendoza, Tigre sacó un empate agónico 2-2 en su visita a Independiente Rivadavia y bajó a su rival del liderato de la tabla anual. Los goles del conjunto mendocino los anotaron Matías Fernández y el paraguayo José Florentín, mientras que para Tigre convirtieron Alan Barrionuevo y Manuel Fernández. "Tanto en este partido como en el anterior con Gimnasia La Plata se nos escapan cuatro puntos en los últimos minutos del partido. Queda un sabor amargo", dijo en conferencia de prensa el director técnico Alfredo Berti. En otros partidos disputados el sábado, Vélez Sarsfield ganó 1-0 a Gimnasia y Esgrima de Mendoza, mismo marcador con el que Lanús venció a Platense, mientras que Rosario Central superó 3-2 a Atlético Tucumán. El viernes, Boca Juniors ganó 2-1 a Talleres de Córdoba, mientras que Instituto de Córdoba superó 1-0 a Defensa y Justicia. La jornada comenzó el jueves con el triunfo 2-1 de Gimnasia y Esgrima La Plata sobre Huracán.

item.title: サッカー＝イプスウィッチ前田、マンＣ戦でプレミア初ゴール
item.description: ［ロンドン １７日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［ロンドン　１７日　ロイター］ - サッカーのイングランド・プレミアリーグは１７日、各地で試合を行い、イプスウィッチの前田大然がマンチェスター・シティー（マンＣ）戦で同リーグでの初ゴールを挙げた。

先発した前田は先制された２分後の前半２１分、右サイドで味方からのパスに追い付き、左足でシュート。開幕から７試合目で待望の初得点をマークした。この後アーリング・ハーランドに２ゴールを決められたイプスウィッチは、後半４５分にＰＫで１点を返したが、２─３で敗戦。前田は後半２６分までプレーした。

ＧＫ鈴木彩艶が所属するアストンビラはニューカッスルに１─０で勝利。鈴木はフル出場を果たし、今季初の完封勝利に貢献した。リバプールはブレントフォードに２─１で逆転勝ち。リバプールの遠藤航はベンチ入りしたが、出場しなかった。

守田英正が所属するハルはフラムに０─１で敗戦。守田は後半３０分から出場した。チェルシーはエバートンに２─０で快勝した。

開幕７連勝のマンＣが勝ち点２１で首位。チェルシーが同１３の４位、リバプールが同１２の暫定５位に浮上した。ハルは９位でイプスウィッチは１０位。今季２勝目を挙げたアストンビラは暫定１２位に上がった。

item.title: サッカー＝バイエルン6ゴール圧勝で暫定首位浮上、伊藤は出番なし
item.description: ［ミュンヘン（ドイツ） １７日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［ミュンヘン（ドイツ）　１７日　ロイター］　 - サッカーのドイツ１部ブンデスリーガは１７日、各地で試合を行い、伊藤洋輝が所属するバイエルン・ミュンヘンがライプチヒを６─１で下し、暫定首位に浮上した。

ホームのバイエルンは前半１２分にルイス・ディアスのゴールで先制すると、前半のうちに３─０とリードを広げ、後半にも立ち上がりの２分にディアスが加点。同８分には、これがブンデスリーガ通算１００試合目の出場となったハリー・ケーンがゴールを挙げ、最後はディアスがハットトリックを達成した。失点は同アディショナルタイムに喫した１点のみだった。

伊藤はこの試合でベンチ入りしたが、最後まで出番はなかった。

佐野海舟がフル出場したマインツは、田中聡フル出場のシャルケに１─０で勝利。マインツの川崎颯太はベンチ入りしなかった。

ドルトムントがウニオン・ベルリンと０─０のドローに終わったため、６試合消化段階でバイエルンが勝ち点１４でドルトムントと並び、得失点差により暫定首位に浮上した。

item.title: ボクシング＝亀田和毅のタイトルマッチ、相手の体調不良で当日中止に
item.description: ［１７日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［１７日　ロイター］ - プロボクシングの亀田和毅（３５）は１７日、米ラスベガスで世界ボクシング協会（ＷＢＡ）世界フェザー級タイトルマッチを行う予定だったが、対戦相手の体調不良により、試合当日に中止となった。米ボクシング専門サイト、ボクシングシーンなどが報じている。

ブランドン・フィゲロア（２９、米国）は１６日の前日計量で規定体重（５７．１５キロ）を２回クリアできず、体重超過でタイトルを剥奪されていた。１回目の計量では約０．６キロのオーバー。１時間後に行われた２回目の計量でも体重は減っていなかった。

亀田はこの試合に勝てば新王者となり、引き分けか負けた場合、王座は空位となる予定だった。亀田の戦績は４２勝５敗。フィゲロアは２６勝２敗１分け。

item.title: Florida State RB Ousmane Kromah carted off with ankle injury
item.description: Florida State running back Ousmane Kromah was carted off with an apparent left ankle injury during the second quarter of Saturday's game at No. 3 Miami.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Florida State running back Ousmane Kromah was carted off with an apparent left ankle injury during the second quarter of Saturday's game at No. 3 Miami. Kromah was headed for the corner of the end zone when he was tackled from behind by Miami linebacker Chase Smith. As he went to the ground, Smith's ankle caught below Him and twisted awkwardly. Kromah got up and tried to hop off the field before going to the ground as the Seminoles' medical staff rushed to treat him. His left leg was placed in an air cast before he was carted to the locker room. Kromah entered Saturday as Florida State's leading rusher with 565 yards and five touchdowns on 100 carries. Kromah had 44 yards on 14 carries on Saturday night before the injury. --Field Level Media

item.title: Carter Verhaeghe’s natural hat trick helps Panthers rout Kraken
item.description: Carter Verhaeghe scored a natural hat trick as the Florida Panthers made NHL history in an 8-3 rout of the visiting Seattle Kraken on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Carter Verhaeghe scored a natural hat trick as the Florida Panthers made NHL history in an 8-3 rout of the visiting Seattle Kraken on Saturday. The Panthers became the first team in NHL history to record natural hat tricks -- three consecutive goals by one player -- in three straight games. Brady Tkachuk accomplished the feat in Florida's previous two outings. Sam Bennett also tallied three times, while Niko Mikkola and Sam Reinhart each had a goal and an assist. Matthew Tkachuk had three helpers, and younger brother Brady Tkachuk added two for the Panthers, who won their third in a row. Goaltender Jacob Markstrom made 20 saves. Shane Wright, Frederick Gaudreau and Ryker Evans scored for Seattle, which finished a five-game trip with a 3-1-1 record. Berkly Catton and Kaapo Kakko each had two assists and Joey Daccord stopped 29 of 37 shots. Bennett opened the scoring at 1:05 of the first period before Wright tied it at 4:54. Verhaeghe snapped a 1-1 tie at 17:56 of the first. The puck squirted free after a battle along the left wing boards and came straight to Verhaeghe just inside the left faceoff dot. He put a one-timer over Daccord's shoulder and into the far upper corner of the net. Verhaeghe tallied again at 19:07 on the power play. The Tkachuks won the puck along the right wing boards and Brady got control in the corner. He took a stride toward the net before firing a pass across the top of the crease to a wide-open Verhaeghe, who lifted the puck over Daccord as the goalie moved from post to post. Verhaeghe scored his third at 6:02 of the second period. Mikkola was stopped on a wraparound attempt but Verhaeghe secured the rebound just outside the left post and slid the puck past the downed Daccord to make it 4-1. The Kraken played without defenseman Brandon Montour, who sustained a lower-body injury Thursday in a 4-3 overtime loss to Tampa Bay. Montour was a member of the Panthers' Stanley Cup-winning team in 2023-24. Mikkola scored just 40 seconds after Verhaeghe completed his hat trick, and Bennett added his second goal at 13:13 of the second period to extend Florida's lead to 6-1. Gaudreau scored for Seattle with 55 seconds remaining in the second period, but Reinhart answered with a power-play goal at 2:25 of the third. Evans cut the deficit to 7-3 at 3:49 before Bennett completed his hat trick at 11:14 to close the scoring. --Field Level Media

item.title: ゴルフ＝竹田は首位と5打差の4位、ビュイックＬＰＧＡ
item.description: ［１７日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［１７日　ロイター］　 - 米女子ゴルフのビュイックＬＰＧＡは１７日、中国・上海の佘山国際ＧＣ（パー７２）で第３ラウンドを行い、竹田麗央は前日の４位をキープした。

竹田は４バーディー、１ダブルボギー、１ボギーの１アンダー７１で回り、通算４アンダーの２１２。ＬＰＧＡツアー初優勝を目指す、首位チェ・ヘジン（韓国）とは５打差となった。

４０位でスタートした吉田優利は６バーディー、１ボギーの５アンダー６７をマーク。通算イーブンパーの９位で、ディフェンディングチャンピオンのジーノ・ティティクル（タイ）らと並んだ。

４位で出た原英莉花は７６とスコアを崩し、通算１オーバーの１４位に後退。勝みなみは通算７オーバーの４０位、西郷真央は通算８オーバーの４６位となった。

item.title: Ryan Blaney’s pole run at Phoenix sets up major Chase opportunity
item.description: AVONDALE, Ariz. -- Score one for the drivers in hot pursuit of Chase leader Kyle Larson.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: AVONDALE, Ariz. -- Score one for the drivers in hot pursuit of Chase leader Kyle Larson. In qualifying for Sunday's 312-lap Freeway Insurance 500 at Phoenix Raceway (3 p.m. ET on USA, MRN and SiriusXM NASCAR Radio), Ryan Blaney claimed the pole position with a lap at 137.143 mph (26.250 seconds). Blaney is one of five drivers closest to Larson in the Chase presented by Mobil 1 standings, and those five drivers earned the top five positions on the grid for Sunday's race, while Larson qualified a disappointing 22nd in Saturday's time trials. Blaney, who is going for his third straight Phoenix win, is fifth in the race for the NASCAR Cup Series title, 85 points behind Larson. His Team Penske teammate, Joey Logano, qualified second at 136.926 mph, 0.032 seconds off Blaney's pace. A four-time Phoenix winner, Logano is sixth in the Chase standings, 92 points in arrears. Joe Gibbs Racing Toyota drivers Chase Briscoe (136.825 mph), Denny Hamlin (136.809 mph) and Christopher Bell (136.617 mph) qualified third through fifth, respectively. Hamlin is second in the standings, 49 points back, with Bell trailing by 51 in third and Briscoe by 65 in fourth. Briscoe is seeking his third straight win in the Chase, having triumphed at Las Vegas Motor Speedway and Charlotte Motor Speedway. Accordingly, Sunday's race presents a golden opportunity for those chasing Larson both to score stage points and compete for a crucial victory. "It's really, really important, just from our side, to put yourself up toward the front early in the race, try to get some points early and try to keep track position," said Blaney, who claimed his fourth Busch Light Pole Award at Phoenix, his fifth of the season and the 17th of his career. "Job one done today, so I'm proud of everybody for doing a good job and taking that first step, and then a whole new challenge tomorrow. Hopefully, we can keep going." Blaney also posted the best single-lap speed in Saturday's practice, covering the one-mile distance in 26.969 seconds (133.487 mph). Three-time series champion Logano described his current Chase position as "pretty desperate." "If we want to win the championship, this race in particular is one that we have circled and has been good for us," he said. "If we're going to make up 90-plus points in four races, you have to win. "It's a must-win scenario and probably multiple times to do that, so if we want to win this whole thing and do it without wishing bad luck upon somebody, then we're going to have to win." Tyler Reddick and Ty Gibbs will start sixth and seventh, as Toyota drivers claimed positions three through seven on the grid. Michael McDowell is the fastest non-Chase driver in eighth, followed by non-Chaser Josh Berry in ninth and Chase driver William Byron in 10th. It's worth noting that in the last 18 Cup races at Phoenix--from 2017 through the entire Gen 7 era--no winner has started deeper in the field than 13th, and all but three winners in that span have started in the top 10. Larson was dissatisfied with the balance of his car throughout the day. He was 13th fastest in practice and 12th in best consecutive 10-lap average. item.title: Woodside natural gas project unit paused after Greenpeace protest off Western Australia
item.description: Woodside said operations remained paused on Sunday at a floating production unit, part of its $12.5 billion Scarborough natural gas project off the coast of Western Australia, due to a Greenpeace protest at the platform.
item.dc:creator: Samuel Mckeith
item.content:encoded: Woodside (WDS.AX) said operations remained paused on Sunday at a floating production unit, part of its $12.5 billion Scarborough natural gas project off the coast of Western Australia, due to a Greenpeace protest at the platform. Two activists from the environmental advocacy group slept overnight on the semi-submersible unit, located around 375 km (233 miles) off the state's northwest coast, in the [USN:L4N46300J TEXT:"protest"] that started on Saturday, Greenpeace said. "Temporary hanging tents" were set up on the unit and the activists would "occupy the platform for as long as possible," Greenpeace said. The group is concerned about the potential impact of Woodside's proposed Browse project on Scott Reef, a remote coral system and foraging area for the endangered pygmy blue whale. Woodside has said it expects no physical contact with the reef above the 75-metre (246-foot) water depth. A Woodside spokesperson said "operations at the Scarborough FPU remain safely paused" on Sunday, a day after temporarily halting pre-commissioning activities as a result of the "unauthorised access". Four activists on Saturday scaled the 70,000 metric ton unit, part of the 98% completed Scarborough project, and displayed banners with the message "Stop Woodside’s Dirty Gas. Save Scott Reef", according to Greenpeace. Australian Border Force on Sunday said it had no update on the incident. It previously said it was working with federal and state agencies on a response.

item.title: US wants Israel to 'crack down' on settler violence in West Bank, Rubio says
item.description: "We're very disturbed by those images and what we're seeing," Marco Rubio said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The United States wants Israel to do more to deter attacks committed by settlers in the West Bank, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Saturday. "We're very disturbed by those images and what we're seeing," Rubio said. "We've asked the Israelis and continue to ask them to crack down on that stuff." His comments to reporters came after the widespread dissemination of video showing multiple individuals attacking Heidi Levine, an American photojournalist with the Washington Post. Levine was one of at least two people injured in the Friday incident, which took place as Israeli settlers [USN:L6N46304S TEXT:"attacked"] Palestinian civilians. European diplomats and a French mayor also were attacked in the occupied West Bank, Belgium's foreign minister said. The US State Department, Rubio said, has inquired about the event that included Levine's attack. Rubio, who spoke to reporters before boarding a flight to Uzbekistan, said he expects to hear back from the US Embassy in Jerusalem by Sunday. Israeli settlers in the West Bank have been involved in at least 170 attacks on Palestinians since September 27, around the start of the annual olive harvest, according to Yesh Din, an Israeli settlements monitoring group.

item.title: Report: Bears QB Caleb Williams to start vs. Falcons
item.description: Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams is expected to return to the starting lineup Sunday against the Falcons in Atlanta after missing the previous three games with a hamstring injury, ESPN and NFL Network reported Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams is expected to return to the starting lineup Sunday against the Falcons in Atlanta after missing the previous three games with a hamstring injury, ESPN and NFL Network reported Saturday. Williams, who has been sidelined since injuring his right hamstring against the Minnesota Vikings on Sept. 20, practiced fully throughout the week without a setback. The Bears officially listed Williams as questionable Friday, but he handled first-team work and continued to progress through the final two practices of the week, according to the reports. Coach Ben Johnson said Friday that Williams was "on track" after the quarterback increased his workload. Chicago went 2-1 without Williams. Case Keenum started a Week 3 victory over the Philadelphia Eagles before Tyson Bagent led the Bears past the New York Jets in Week 4 and started last week's loss to the Green Bay Packers. Williams has completed 36 of 55 passes for 407 yards, two touchdowns and one interception in two games this season. He also has rushed for 107 yards and two scores. The injury ended a run of 36 consecutive regular-season starts for Williams dating to the beginning of his NFL career. His return sets up the first NFL meeting between Williams and Atlanta quarterback Michael Penix Jr., two of the six quarterbacks selected in the first round of the 2024 NFL Draft. Chicago took Williams first overall, while the Falcons selected Penix at No. 8. Penix also dealt with an injury this week after hurting his ribs in Atlanta's Week 5 loss to Baltimore. The Bears (3-2) will try to rebound from their loss at Green Bay against the Falcons (2-3). --Field Level Media

item.title: Lightning rally from 2 down to beat Canucks
item.description: Jake Guentzel scored the tiebreaking goal in the third period as the Tampa Bay Lightning kept their home slate clean with a 4-2 comeback win over the Vancouver Canucks on Saturday afternoon.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Jake Guentzel scored the tiebreaking goal in the third period as the Tampa Bay Lightning kept their home slate clean with a 4-2 comeback win over the Vancouver Canucks on Saturday afternoon. Guentzel, who also had an assist, gave Tampa Bay its first lead at 2:04 of the third period when his long shot deflected off the stick of Vancouver's Liam Ohgren for his fourth goal of the season. Pontus Holmberg added an insurance goal with just over four minutes left as the Lightning improved to 5-0-0 at home by potting four unanswered goals. Nikita Kucherov tallied twice, and Brayden Point had two assists. Goaltender Dennis Hildeby made 12 saves. Linus Karlsson and center Elias Pettersson netted for the Canucks, who finished 0-5-1 on their East Coast road trip. Goalie Kevin Lankinen, who entered with a 6.88 goals-against average, stopped 31 shots. As the Florida Panthers did against Vancouver on Thursday, Tampa Bay controlled play and generated early scoring chances but struggled to beat the opposing goalie. Vancouver did not register its first shot on Hildeby until Elias Pettersson put one on goal at 6:53. In his club's best chance early, Guentzel had a wide-open cage on an odd-man rush, but Lankinen stretched out and made a sprawling kick save at 9:02 to keep it scoreless. Just after a Kucherov penalty for tripping expired, Filip Chytil worked the puck behind Hildeby's net and found Paul Cotter, who delivered an off-balance pass to Karlsson. The winger scored his second goal of the season at 15:32 to give the Canucks a 1-0 lead. On Vancouver's second power play, Pettersson made it 2-0 with a shot from nearly no angle to Hildeby's left. The attempt caromed in off the goalie at 4:35 for Pettersson's third tally of the year. Kucherov answered less than two minutes later on the Lightning's first power play of the game and added another right off a faceoff nearly five minutes later to knot it 2. The score remained tied through 40 minutes despite the Lightning holding a 26-12 advantage in shots. --Field Level Media

item.title: Packers place WR Skyy Moore, two others on IR
item.description: The Green Bay Packers placed wide receiver Skyy Moore and defensive tackles Javon Hargrave and Jonathan Ford on injured reserve Saturday in advance of the team's game against the visiting Dallas Cowboys on Sunday night.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Green Bay Packers placed wide receiver Skyy Moore and defensive tackles Javon Hargrave and Jonathan Ford on injured reserve Saturday in advance of the team's game against the visiting Dallas Cowboys on Sunday night. All three players previously had been ruled out against Dallas and now must miss at least four games under NFL injured reserve rules. Hargrave suffered an Achilles injury late in Sunday's 31-7 victory over the Chicago Bears and is expected to miss the remainder of the season. Moore has a high ankle sprain and Ford a calf injury. Moore has seven catches for 35 yards in five games this season for Green Bay (3-2). In other moves Saturday, the Packers activated wide receiver Savion Williams from IR and elevated defensive end Arron Mosby and wide receiver Coleman Owen from the practice squad. Williams has not played this season but caught 10 passes for 78 yards and a touchdown in 12 games for the Packers last year. --Field Level Media

item.title: Seattle Reign lose young star Maddie Dahlien (knee) for rest of season
item.description: Seattle Reign FC placed forward Maddie Dahlien on the season-ending injury list Saturday after she suffered an ACL tear while training with the United States' under-23 women's national team.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Seattle Reign FC placed forward Maddie Dahlien on the season-ending injury list Saturday after she suffered an ACL tear while training with the United States' under-23 women's national team. Dahlien, 22, has three goals and four assists in 25 appearances for Seattle this season. The assists tie her for the team lead. She was one of three finalists for NWSL Rookie of the Year in 2025. "We're heartbroken for Maddie, and our priority is making sure she has the support and resources she needs throughout her recovery," Seattle general manager Lesle Gallimore said in a news release. "She has made a tremendous impact on this club in just two seasons, and her competitive drive, determination and work ethic are evident in everything she does. We're confident she'll approach this challenge with that same mentality and come back stronger." Dahlien was a member of North Carolina's 2024 national championship team in college and quickly excelled with Seattle. She had four goals and four assists in 2025. Dahlien made three appearances with the U.S. women's national team earlier this year. She earned her first cap in January against Paraguay. During this month's under-23 training camp, Dahlien started in a 5-0 victory over the Dominican Republic on Oct. 9 in Fayetteville, Ga. Four days later, she entered in the 58th minute and left 16 minutes later as the U.S. beat the Dominican Republic 6-2, also in Fayetteville. --Field Level Media

item.title: Hurricanes win 7th straight, defeat Jets
item.description: Nikolaj Ehlers scored the go-ahead power-play goal in the third period as the Carolina Hurricanes rallied for their seventh straight victory, defeating the host Winnipeg Jets 3-2 on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Nikolaj Ehlers scored the go-ahead power-play goal in the third period as the Carolina Hurricanes rallied for their seventh straight victory, defeating the host Winnipeg Jets 3-2 on Saturday. Ehlers put Carolina ahead 3-2 with a power-play slap shot from the high slot at 6:43 of the third period for his first of the season. Mark Jankowski and Jesperi Kotkaniemi also scored, and Shayne Gostisbehere had two assists for the Hurricanes. Pyotr Kochetkov made 21 saves and improved to 5-0-0 on the season. Mark Scheifele and Alex Iafallo scored for the Jets, who have lost two straight games and three of their last four. Clay Stevenson made 34 saves. The Jets outshot the Hurricanes 10-8 in the first period. Carolina didn't register its first shot on goal until the 5:26 mark. Scheifele put Winnipeg ahead 1-0 at 4:23 of the second period on a backhanded shot. It was also the Jets' first shot of the period and extended Scheifele's points streak to five games. Jankowski tied the game 1-1 at 8:19 when Logan Stankoven set him up for a wrist shot through traffic on the power play. Iafallo gave the Jets a 2-1 lead at 10:59 when Adam Lowry intercepted Kochetkov's attempt to play the puck behind the net and set him up for a tap-in. Kotkaniemi knotted the score back up 2-2 at 16:50 when he tipped in Gostisbehere's shot from the blue line. Overall, Carolina won 55.2% of the faceoffs, and they outpaced Winnipeg in takeaways 6-4. Most importantly, they put a lot more pressure on the net with 37 shots compared to the Jets' 23 attempts. The Jets have now lost back-to-back games; they suffered a 4-3 overtime loss to the Chicago Blackhawks on Thursday. They will travel to St. Louis to take on the Blues on Tuesday. Meanwhile, Carolina is scheduled to face the Calgary Flames on the road on Sunday. --Field Level Media

item.title: WNBA Commissioner Engelbert says successor needs 'thick skin'
item.description: WNBA Commissioner Cathy Engelbert said on Saturday her successor will need to have "very thick skin" to navigate the job as she prepares to retire at the end of the year.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: WNBA Commissioner Cathy Engelbert said on Saturday her successor will need to have "very thick skin" to navigate the job as she prepares to retire at the end of the year. Engelbert announced her [USN:L6N44W0YL TEXT:"retirement"] last month after seven years in the role during which she guided the league through a historic labor agreement and massive franchise expansion. "It's like a multidimensional role. You have to have very thick skin," Engelbert told a press conference in San Francisco, ahead of Game 1 of the WNBA Finals between the Golden State Valkyries and Atlanta Dream. "You have to have confidence that we can continue this growth trajectory and confidence in building relationships with players and agents and the Board of Governors, the owners and the stakeholders." Engelbert said the league has hired a search firm to find her replacement and there has been a lot of interest in the job. She also offered advice to her successor about the next steps for the league. "When I came in, the first question I had was ... what's our strategy?" she said. "We did a very simple three-tiered strategy, which was player first, stakeholder success and fan engagement, fan experience. "I would say that strategy has worked. And now you do have to evaluate whether there's other aspects of that where we really need to broaden our platform. "I would tell the next commissioner that we've got to continue that and get into a sustained growth period at the league office. Then the teams are still in hypergrowth, and support the teams in their growth objectives because teams have grown a lot."

item.title: Venezuela expects nearly $76 billion in oil investment over five years, acting president says
item.description: Venezuela expects nearly $76 billion in oil investment over the next five years under recently signed agreements, acting President Delcy Rodriguez said on Saturday, adding that a bilateral accord with the US includes plans to drill 250 rigs.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Venezuela expects nearly $76 billion in oil investment over the next five years under recently signed agreements, acting President Delcy Rodriguez said on Saturday, adding that a bilateral accord with the US includes plans to drill 250 rigs. Since the January ouster of President Nicolas Maduro, the country has been reopening its energy sector to foreign investment with the backing of the administration of US President Donald Trump. The deals could help revive output in Venezuela, which has the world's largest proven crude oil reserves but produces well below levels seen a decade ago. Rodriguez said on national television the investments would bring direct benefits to Venezuela while also benefiting its partners, adding that the bilateral agreement with the US covers 17 oil fields and formed part of a broader package of 61 agreements signed by the parties. "Major investments are coming," she said. "We are talking about investment of almost $76 billion over five years. Those investments will translate into direct benefits for our country in a win-win partnership, because our partner will also benefit." Rodriguez also highlighted a recovery in oil production in western Zulia state. There, production rose from 70,000 barrels per day (bpd) to 370,000 bpd, she said, adding it was expected to reach 400,000 bpd by the end of the year. She did not say over what period the increase occurred. Venezuela's oil output has suffered from years of underinvestment, operational problems at state oil company PDVSA and US sanctions on the energy sector.

item.title: Two killed, including 6-year-old, when truck drives through Kansas youth soccer game, police say
item.description: A truck drove into a youth soccer game in Wichita, Kansas, leaving a six-year-old boy and a 35-year-old man dead, and 10 others hospitalized with traumatic injuries, police said on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Karen Freifeld, Jasper Ward
item.content:encoded: A truck drove into a youth soccer game in Wichita, Kansas, leaving a six-year-old boy and a 35-year-old man dead, and 10 others hospitalized with traumatic injuries, police said on Saturday. The injuries ranged from minor to severe, but none appear to be life threatening, Wichita police Captain Aaron Moses said at a news conference. The two people killed were pronounced dead at the scene, he said. Moses said a 34-year-old woman was driving the truck, which ended up in a field at the west end of the Stryker Sports Complex. She has been cooperating with investigators, he said, but when asked whether she had been arrested, he said only that she was in custody. "We know what happened, but now we're working very hard to find out why it happened, and we're not there yet," Wichita police Chief Joe Sullivan said. The injured include two youths aged 5, two aged 8, a 9-year-old and five adults, police said. In addition to those 10 people, one adult was hospitalized for non-traumatic medical issues. The driver had a child playing soccer at the complex, but not on the field where the incident took place, Moses said. The truck involved had two juveniles as passengers, he said. Emergency dispatchers started getting calls about the incident at 3:25 p.m. local time (2025 GMT), Moses said. "Today is a heartbreaking day for Wichita," Mayor Lily Wu said. "Families came to Stryker Sports Complex to enjoy a Saturday afternoon, watching their children play soccer and no one could have imagined the tragedy that would unfold."

item.title: Dubois defeats Wardley in short order to retain WBO heavyweight title
item.description: 'Dynamite' Daniel Dubois retained his WBO heavyweight belt with a one-sided and devastating second-round stoppage of fellow Briton Fabio Wardley in their world title rematch on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: 'Dynamite' Daniel Dubois retained his WBO heavyweight belt with a one-sided and devastating second-round stoppage of fellow Briton Fabio Wardley in their world title rematch on Saturday. The 29-year-old champion made a storming start at London's O2 Arena and Wardley's legs went from under him for a count within 17 seconds of the opening bell as Dubois floored him with a straight right. Wardley, 31, beat the count and could have been stopped at the end of the first round when he took a further brutal pounding on the ropes but was saved by the bell. There was no escape from the onslaught of blows in the second with Dubois picking up where he left off and Wardley taking punch after punch until the towel was thrown in and referee Steve Gray brought the fight to a close. "Fabio is a great warrior, coming in for a second time, but it was my time and my era," said 'Triple D', never a man for long speeches. "I had my intentions, bad intentions, from the beginning. "Our back was against the wall the first time, this time we just had to go out there and show that we mean business and that's what we did tonight." HRGOVIC READY TO PUT HIS TITLE ON THE LINE Dubois dealt Wardley his first defeat as a professional when he came back from two knockdowns, the first after 16 seconds, to take the title in the 11th round of a thunderous and bloody clash [USN:L6N41M07R TEXT:"in Manchester last May."] Wardley, promoted to WBO champion last November after Ukraine's Oleksandr Usyk vacated the title, was acclaimed for his courage and refusal to give in first time around but on Saturday he looked a shell of the man seen in Manchester. He now has a 20-2-1 record with Dubois on 24 wins with three defeats. "I've always thrown myself in with the best competitors out there, the toughest, the biggest, hardest, meanest guys around. There's no shame in testing yourself against the best," he said. "Daniel's a testament to coming up short and coming again, I'll be looking to do the exact same thing. "Boxing is a game of fine margins. It can be done and over in a round or two or it can go into a big old war like it was last time." Dubois was previously the IBF champion, [USN:L1N3TG065 TEXT:"losing it to Usyk in London in July last year"] before coming back to take the WBO belt from Wardley. Croatian Filip Hrgovic, [USN:L6N44Q078 TEXT:"the IBF champion after beating Britain's Moses Itauma in August,"] was ringside on Saturday and challenged Dubois to a fight with both belts on the line. "It was an easy night for Daniel. He did a good job, quick win. So he's ready to fight me in March, right Daniel?," said Hrgovic, before promoter Frank Warren suggested he might have to deal with other candidates first. Dubois beat the Croatian in June 2024 to take the interim IBF belt and was then upgraded to champion when Usyk vacated his title. "I want to have a rematch with him, I want to get my old belt back and rule the division," said Dubois.

item.title: Top 25 roundup: Auburn knocks off No. 1 Georgia on day of upsets
item.description: Alex McPherson made a 34-yard field goal as time expired to lift visiting Auburn to a shocking 27-24 victory over No. 1 Georgia on Saturday in Athens.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Alex McPherson made a 34-yard field goal as time expired to lift visiting Auburn to a shocking 27-24 victory over No. 1 Georgia on Saturday in Athens. Bulldogs quarterback Gunner Stockton had three turnovers, including a fumble with 58 seconds left to give the Tigers the ball at their 44-yard line. After Gabe Harris Jr.'s roughing-the-passer penalty on the ensuing drive, McPherson gave Auburn (4-2, 2-2 Southeastern Conference) its first win over Georgia since 2017 and first in Athens in 21 years. Byrum Brown threw for 150 yards and a touchdown, adding 115 rushing yards and a score for the Tigers, who trailed by 14 points in the first quarter. He completed 15 of 26 passes. Wide receiver Christian Neptune also completed a TD pass to Keshaun Singleton. Stockton, who connected on 22 of 34 passing attempts, threw for 272 yards and two touchdowns, but had two interceptions for Georgia (6-1, 4-1), which suffered its first loss to an unranked team since 2019. London Humphreys and Lawson Luckie caught TD passes, while Dwight Phillips Jr. rushed for 68 yards and a score. No. 8 BYU 28, No. 2 Notre Dame 24 Bear Bachmeier passed for a touchdown, caught a touchdown pass and rushed for two more as the Cougars held on in the final seconds for a win over the Fighting Irish in Provo, Utah. Walker Lyons hauled in a go-ahead 6-yard touchdown pass with 1:47 remaining to lift BYU (6-0). Bachmeier completed 23 of 36 passes for 224 yards, the one touchdown and one interception, and he rushed 13 times for 45 yards and the two scores. CJ Carr completed 27 of 49 passes for 261 yards for Notre Dame (6-1). Nolan James Jr. and Jonaz Walton rushed for one touchdown apiece. No. 3 Miami 43, Florida State 35 (2 OT) Malachi Toney made the go-ahead touchdown reception and then threw the ensuing two-point conversion pass to lift the Hurricanes to a double-overtime victory over the Seminoles in Miami Gardens, Fla. Toney caught 11 of his 12 targets for 154 yards and two touchdowns and ran for 31 yards on two carries to help Miami (6-0, 4-0 Atlantic Coast Conference) stave off an upset bid by Florida State (3-4, 1-3). Hurricanes quarterback Darian Mensah completed 23 of 34 passes for 326 yards, three touchdowns and one interception. Ashton Daniels went 15 of 28 for 298 yards, four touchdowns and one interception to lead the Seminoles, who lost leading rusher Ousmane Kromah to an apparent injury in the second quarter. No. 4 Ohio State 19, No. 5 Indiana 15 Jeremiah Smith was bottled up for three quarters, but his 38-yard touchdown catch in the fourth quarter helped the Buckeyes hold off the Hoosiers in Big Ten action in Bloomington, Ind. The Hoosiers (6-1, 3-1) had their 22-game winning streak end when a fourth-and-4 pass at the Ohio State 27-yard line was incomplete when Nick Marsh stepped out of bounds in the end zone while making the catch with 1:02 left. Ohio State (6-1, 4-0) led 13-7 early in the fourth when, on fourth-and-1 from the Indiana 38, Smith recorded his 39th career receiving touchdown to tie Michigan's Braylon Edwards for the Big Ten record. The two-point conversion failed as the Buckeyes led 19-7 lead with 12:46 remaining, but Indiana responded with a 19-yard catch by Marsh from Josh Hoover and a two-point pass to Turbo Richard to make it 19-15. Smith had four catches for 68 yards. Julian Sayin was 15 of 29 for 235 yards with a TD and two interceptions before being injured in the fourth. He was sporting a sling late in the game and Buckeyes coach Ryan Day said Sayin would miss several weeks. No. 14 Tennessee 26, No. 6 Alabama 10 DeSean Bishop ran for two touchdowns and the Volunteers' stifling defense paved the way to a win over the Crimson Tide in the "Third Saturday in October" rivalry in Knoxville, Tenn. Bishop ran for 159 yards, with 97 of those and both of his scores coming after halftime. Tennessee quarterback George MacIntyre completed 21 of 31 passes for 197 yards and one interception, and Cooper Ranvier made all four of his field goal attempts for Tennessee (6-1, 3-1 SEC). The Volunteers have won three straight home games against Alabama after losing seven consecutive at home and 15 straight overall in the rivalry from 2007-21. Alabama quarterback Keelon Russell was 19 of 29 for 147 yards and two interceptions, matching his total from the first six games of the season. Alabama (5-2, 3-2) managed just 201 yards of offense and had four turnovers, losing consecutive regular-season games for the first time since it dropped the final games of the 2007 regular season. Florida 27, No. 7 Texas 24 Tramell Jones Jr. passed for 155 yards and a pair of touchdowns in his first career start, as the Gators scored 24 unanswered points on the way to a 27-24 win over the host Longhorns in Austin. Florida (5-2, 3-2) also got 91 yards on 25 carries from Jadan Baugh, including an 11-yard TD run with 6:22 remaining to put the Gators up 27-17. Lakota Dippre caught only two passes, but both went for touchdowns, covering 7 and 8 yards, respectively. Texas' Arch Manning hit Cam Coleman for a 9-yard scoring pass with 4:21 left to cut into the deficit. The Longhorns (4-2, 1-2) had another chance to tie or win the game, but Manning fumbled when he was sacked by Florida's Myles Graham. Kanye Clark fell on the ball with 1:58 to play. Manning finished with 173 yards passing, completing 14 of 20 attempts. No. 9 Ole Miss 31, No. 13 Missouri 3 Trinidad Chambliss threw three touchdown passes and rushed for another score as the Rebels dominated on defense in a runaway win over the Tigers in Oxford, Miss. Kewan Lacy gained 122 rushing yards on 16 carries for the Rebels despite missing multiple drives because of an injured hamstring. Makhi Frazier added 101 rushing yards on 15 carries for Ole Miss, which scored the final 31 points. The Rebels (5-1, 3-1 SEC) limited Missouri halfback Jamal Roberts to 39 rushing yards on 20 carries after he had rushed for over 200 yards in each of the previous two games. The Tigers (5-2, 2-2) finished the game with 10 straight scoreless possessions after Blake Craig kicked a short field goal on their opening drive. Austin Simmons, facing his former team where he began the 2025 season as the starter, completed 25 of 44 passes for 339 yards but with no touchdowns and an interception. No. 10 Texas Tech 53, Arizona State 25 The Red Raiders generated 502 yards of total offense behind the passing of Will Hammond and running of J'Koby Williams in a 53-25 Big 12 victory over the Sun Devils in Lubbock, Texas. Hammond completed 18 of 26 passes for 232 yards with one touchdown and no interceptions. Williams rushed for a career-high 165 yards on 11 carries with two touchdowns, which tied a career-high. Kenny Johnson had seven receptions for a career-high 120 yards for Texas Tech (6-0, 3-0 Big 12). Quarterback Mikey Keene relieved starter Cutter Boley for Arizona State (3-3, 1-2) in the second half and completed 25 of 34 passes for 256 yards with two TDs and no interceptions. Boley threw a 74-yard first half TD to Raiden Vines-Bright. The running game mustered only 35 yards on 28 carries. No. 11 Utah 27, Colorado 24 Devon Dampier tossed three touchdown passes, two to Braden Pegan, to help the Utes edge hold off the Buffaloes in Big 12 play at Boulder, Colo. Hunter Andrews also had a scoring reception and James Chenault Jr. made a key interception for Utah (6-0, 3-0 Big 12). The Utes stretched their winning streak to 12 games, the longest active streak in FBS after Indiana and Notre Dame lost earlier Saturday. Wayshawn Parker rushed for 98 yards on 23 carries, and Dampier completed 24 of 41 passes for 278 yards and was intercepted twice. Isaac Wilson, a former Utah starting quarterback, completed 18 of 30 passes for 256 yards, two touchdowns and two interceptions for Colorado (2-4, 0-3). JaQuail Smith caught a touchdown pass and had 141 scrimmage yards (73 rushing, 68 receiving) for the Buffaloes, who dropped their fourth straight game. No. 12 UCLA 17, Wisconsin 7 Anthony Woods and Wayne Knight each scored a goal-line touchdown, and the Bruins bottled up the Badgers to remain unbeaten with a victory in Pasadena, Calif. UCLA (6-0, 4-0 Big Ten) scored on drives of 84, 91 and 89 yards, with Ty Dieffenbach leading the offense. Dieffenbach, who finished the Bruins' Oct. 10 win at Oregon, made his first career start in place of the injured Nico Iamaleava. He completed 22 of 33 passes for 264 yards and one interception, spreading the ball among eight receivers. Wisconsin (4-2, 2-1) forced UCLA to rely more heavily on the passing game, focusing on limiting a Bruins rushing attack that ranked sixth nationally at 253.2 yards per game. UCLA held Wisconsin to 214 yards of total offense, including 66 passing yards by Colton Joseph, who completed 6 of 16 attempts. No. 15 Kentucky 21, Oklahoma 13 Jordan Castell had a pair of interceptions, including one he returned for a touchdown with just more than a minute remaining, to lift the Wildcats to a win over the Sooners in Norman, Okla. Oklahoma needed to drive 75 yards for a touchdown and a two-point conversion to keep the game alive. The Sooners quickly moved the ball near midfield, but Ty Bryant picked off Oklahoma quarterback John Mateer with 21 seconds remaining to put the game away. Oklahoma (3-3, 1-2 SEC) outgained the Wildcats 346-230 but couldn't overcome the 4-0 turnover deficit. Kentucky quarterback Kenny Minchey finished 21 of 28 for 158 yards and two touchdowns, both to tight end Willie Rodriguez. Former Oklahoma wide receiver Nic Anderson had five catches for 48 yards to lead Kentucky (6-1, 4-1), which has won five straight games and four consecutive conference games. No. 20 Houston 35, No. 18 Oklahoma State 32 Conner Weigman threw for 343 yards and five touchdowns to lead the Cougars to a victory over the visiting Cowboys in a Big 12 shootout. Weigman completed 24 of 33 passes with one interception. Houston's Amare Thomas caught seven passes for 126 yards and two touchdowns, while Trent Walker had seven receptions for 104 yards and a score for the Cougars (6-1, 3-1 Big 12). Oklahoma State quarterback Drew Mestemaker passed for 365 yards with three touchdowns and an interception, Caleb Hawkins caught seven passes for 125 yards and a touchdown, Wyatt Young had 99 receiving yards and a score and Justin Bowick also caught a touchdown pass for the Cowboys (4-2, 2-1). No. 21 Wake Forest 41, California 7 Gio Lopez threw three of his four touchdown passes to Dominick Barry, and the Demon Deacons roll past the Golden Bears in Berkeley, Calif. Wake Forest (6-1, 4-1 Atlantic Coast Conference), playing with a national ranking for the first time this season, moved into second place in the league. Lopez threw for 267 yards on 16-of-23 passing and added 51 yards rushing. Barry, a freshman who had not scored previously, finished with 102 receiving yards on four catches. Jackson Brousseau completed 17 of 29 passes for just 81 yards for Cal (3-4, 2-2). Former starter Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele entered late and threw a 28-yard touchdown pass to Mason Mini with 8:29 remaining for the Golden Bears' first points. Sagapolutele finished with 110 passing yards. No. 22 LSU 31, No. 16 Mississippi State 0 Sam Leavitt passed for 289 yards and four touchdowns as the Tigers routed the Bulldogs in Baton Rouge, La. Leavitt, who entered the game with an SEC-worst eight interceptions, threw none against Mississippi State as he completed 31 of 38 passes. Jackson Harris caught two touchdown passes for the Tigers (5-2, 2-2 SEC), whose defense stopped all five of the short-handed Bulldogs' fourth-down attempts. Mississippi State (4-2, 2-2) was without quarterback Kamario Taylor, the SEC leader in passing touchdowns and yards per game, and leading rusher Fluff Bothwell, both because of injuries. Redshirt freshman Billy Puckett started in place of Taylor and threw for 121 yards and an interception on 16-of-26 passing. No. 24 SMU 23, Virginia 13 Kevin Jennings passed for 246 yards and two touchdowns to lead the host Mustangs past the Cavaliers in Dallas. Jennings' second touchdown pass, a 37-yarder to Jalen Hale early in the fourth quarter that provided the game's final margin, tied him with Ben Hicks (2016-18) for second place in school history with 71 career touchdown passes, one shy of the record set by Tanner Mordecai (2021-22). Jennings finished 23-for-36 with no interceptions. Kendrick Raphael rushed for 124 yards, Yannick Smith had five catches for 87 yards, and former SMU soccer player Brendan Baird kicked the first three field goals of his career as the Mustangs (5-1, 3-1 ACC) improved to 10-0 at home in conference play since joining in 2024. Beau Pribula had 137 yards on 13-of-22 passing and ran for 25 yards and a touchdown for Virginia (4-3, 2-2), which fell to 0-3 away from home this season. Will Bettridge kicked a pair of field goals for Virginia's other points. No. 25 Northwestern 24, Michigan State 21 Jackson Kleather's 34-yard field goal with 2 seconds remaining lifted the Wildcats to a comeback win over the Spartans in East Lansing, Mich. Northwestern (5-1, 2-1 Big Ten) prevented an upset by Michigan State (2-5, 0-4) and former Wildcats coach Pat Fitzgerald when Matthew Smith blocked a go-ahead field-goal attempt from 33 yards by Liam Boyd with one minute left in the fourth quarter. Northwestern then drove 64 yards to set up Kleather's game-winning kick. Aidan Chiles completed 18 of 27 passes for 226 yards, and Caleb Komolafe ran for 67 yards and a touchdown on 15 carries for the Wildcats, who are ranked for the first time since 2020. Alessio Milivojevic completed 19 of 30 passes for 216 yards and two touchdowns for the Spartans. --Field Level Media

item.title: Kenya confirms four new Ebola cases, bringing total number to seven
item.description: The cases are the first known infections passed on inside Kenya, where the first patient arrived from Congo on Oct 3.
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:
Advertisement

World

Kenya confirms four new Ebola cases, bringing total number to seven

The cases are the first known infections passed on inside Kenya, where the first patient arrived from Congo on Oct 3.

A tent which has been erected to screen travellers within the health port services at the Malaba crossing-point between Kenya and Uganda after a man who had been living in the Democratic Republic of Congo travelled and died of a new Ebola outbreak involving the Bundibugyo species at the Nairobi Hospital, in Malaba, Kenya Oct 8, 2026. (Photo: REUTERS/Jackson Adika)

18 Oct 2026 04:52AM

Kenya confirmed four new cases of the Ebola Bundibugyo virus on Saturday (Oct 17), including three health workers who treated the country's first patient, bringing the total number of confirmed cases to seven, the health ministry said. The other new case is a male relative of the index patient, who died. The relative had been in quarantine since Oct 6, the ministry said in a statement. The cases are the first known infections passed on inside Kenya, where the first patient arrived from Congo on Oct 3. But the ministry says it has traced and quarantined nearly all of his contacts and there is no evidence that the virus is spreading in the community . The three health workers, two men and a woman aged 29, 35 and 32 respectively, managed the index case on Oct 3 and 4 and had been in quarantine since Oct 9, it said. All four new patients were already in quarantine when they developed symptoms and were diagnosed.

The second and third patients confirmed earlier are stable and responding well to supportive treatment, the ministry said. It said 128 of 130 listed contacts, or 98.5 percent, had been traced and placed in quarantine, higher than the 85 percent global benchmark it said was needed to break the chain of transmission. Kenya's cases are linked to the Ebola epidemic in Congo, the second-largest outbreak ever recorded, with more than 9,000 cases and more than 4,000 deaths.

Related:

Tan Kiat How on low risk of Ebola cross-border transmission to Singapore

WHO says Congo Ebola outbreak can still be brought under control within three months

Commentary: This Ebola outbreak should never have caught the world off guard

There are no approved vaccines or treatments for the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola. The first Kenyan case was a man who had been ill in Congo for about a month before travelling by road to Uganda and flying to Nairobi on Oct 3. He died on Oct 5. His arrival has raised concerns about screening at the Congo-Uganda border, which has been closed since May, and at Nairobi's Jomo Kenyatta International Airport. Efforts to trace the remaining two contacts were ongoing, the ministry said. "The risk to the general public remains low as there is no evidence of community transmission," it said, adding that there were no restrictions on travel, trade or public gatherings.

Source: Reuters/fs

item.title: ローマ教皇が退院、肺腺がん手術後の検査良好 日曜の祈りに参加へ
item.description:
Joshua McElwee
[バチカン市 １７日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Joshua McElwee

[バチカン市 １７日 ロイター] - 肺腺がんの手術を受けたローマ教皇レオ１４世が１７日、入院していたローマの病院を退院した。教皇庁（バチカン）によると、１８日の日曜の祈りに参加する予定という。

教皇はローマのジェメリ病院の外で手を振って見送りの人々に応えながら、自力で歩いて待機していた車に向かった。

教皇は１３日に、がん組織を全て除去するため右肺の下葉を切除する手術を受けた。手術後の経過は良好で１６日にはロシアのプーチン大統領と電話会談していた。

医師団は１７日、血液検査や胸部画像検査を行った結果、教皇は退院できる状態にあり、日常の活動も自立して行うことができると述べた。

教皇は１１月６─１７日にウルグアイ、アルゼンチン、ペルーを訪問する予定。

item.title: Prominent Guatemalan anti-corruption lawyer killed in shooting
item.description: Guatemalan lawyer Juan Francisco Solorzano Foppa, known for his high-profile fight against corruption in the Central American country, died after being shot on Saturday by two men while visiting a sports center in Guatemala City, a crime condemned by President Bernardo Arevalo.
item.dc:creator: Sofia Menchu
item.content:encoded: Guatemalan lawyer Juan Francisco Solorzano Foppa, known for his high-profile fight against corruption in the Central American country, died after being shot on Saturday by two men while visiting a sports center in Guatemala City, a crime condemned by President Bernardo Arevalo. Solorzano Foppa was a 43-year-old former prosecutor and anti-corruption lawyer who denounced wrongdoing by some of Guatemala's most powerful politicians, business leaders and companies, and in 2023 briefly joined the defense team of a prominent journalist. Shortly after the attack, Guatemalan police reported that they had detained two men and seized a carbine-style firearm and a motorcycle. According to the police, the arrests and seizure of the weapon were in connection with the case. "I strongly condemn the cowardly murder of former prosecutor Juan Francisco Solorzano Foppa. Both the direct perpetrators and those who ordered the crime must face the full weight of the law," Arevalo said on his official X account. He added that he had instructed his government to coordinate with the relevant authorities to solve the crime. "Those who believe that terror can intimidate the people of Guatemala and the government I lead are mistaken. In honor of Foppa, in honor of our homeland, in honor of justice." The lawyer was known for his anti-corruption work as head of the Criminal Investigations Directorate within the Public Prosecutor's Office, and later as head of Guatemala's tax authority, the SAT, from 2016 to 2018, when he helped prosecute dozens of powerful Guatemalan business figures and recover unpaid taxes. In 2025, Solorzano Foppa alleged a connection between the Barrio 18 gang and the National Unity of Hope party, as well as links between criminal gangs and the judicial system. In 2023, he briefly joined the defense team of Guatemalan journalist Jose Ruben Zamora, who has become an international symbol of resistance to the criminalization of journalism and the erosion of judicial independence in Central America. Solorzano Foppa had to leave the Zamora case after being accused by the Public Prosecutor's Office of obstructing the proceedings and destroying or concealing information, a charge he denied but ultimately accepted as part of a plea agreement, saying he did not believe he would receive a fair trial.

item.title: Capitals score 4 straight goals, double up Devils
item.description: Ilya Protas scored the tiebreaking goal early in the second period Saturday afternoon for the host Washington Capitals, who rode a four-goal surge to a 4-2 win over the New Jersey Devils.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Ilya Protas scored the tiebreaking goal early in the second period Saturday afternoon for the host Washington Capitals, who rode a four-goal surge to a 4-2 win over the New Jersey Devils. Ryan Leonard scored in the first before Dylan Strome and Boone Jenner added goals in the second for the Capitals, who have won two straight. Goaltender Logan Thompson made 29 saves. Arseny Gritsyuk had a goal in the first and Timo Meier scored in the final minute of the third for the Devils, whose two-game winning streak ended. Goalie Jake Allen recorded 21 saves as New Jersey sustained its fourth multi-goal defeat of the season. The Devils opened the scoring just after a power play expired at the 10:04 mark of the first, when Gritsyuk's shot from behind the left faceoff circle clipped off Thompson and trickled into the net. The Capitals tied the score six minutes later with a power-play goal fueled by Leonard's impressive effort. Leonard took a drop pass from Jakob Chychrun in front of the Washington net, raced up the ice, weaved between the Devils' Evan Rodrigues and Luke Hughes and shifted the puck before burying it into the right corner of the net with 3:18 left. Protas gave the Capitals the lead for good by capping another end-to-end rush 1:16 into the second. Alex Ovechkin sent a pass beyond the reach of Devils defenseman Jonas Siegenthaler and over the stick of Stefan Noesen to Protas, who sent a shot over Allen's glove shoulder. The Capitals padded the lead just 3:20 later. Strome and Jordan Kyrou exchanged the puck between the faceoff circles before Kyrou fed Strome at the edge of the crease, where the center shuffled the puck before flicking a shot over the glove of a sprawling Allen. Jenner closed out the decisive outburst with 8:46 left in the second period. Vincent Desharnais' shot from above the right faceoff circle glanced off the stick of Devils defenseman Johnathan Kovacevic to Jenner, who beat Allen from point-blank range. The Devils were 0-for-3 on the power play before Meier scored a power-play tally with 19 seconds left in the game. --Field Level Media

item.title: Ukrainian foreign minister says Russian-held town is a 'death trap' with starving residents
item.description: Andrii Sybiha urged international organizations to help evacuate residents.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said on Saturday that Russian occupying forces were turning the Ukrainian town of Oleshky into a "death trap" gripped by starvation, and urged international organisations to help evacuate its residents. Sybiha made his comments on X a day after Russian President Vladimir Putin pledged, in a [USN:L8N4621IK TEXT:"conversation with Pope Leo"], to cooperate in delivering vital supplies into the town in southern Ukraine's Kherson region. "Russians are trying to turn the Ukrainian town of Oleshky into a death trap. The hospital has run out of medicine. Dozens of bodies lie in the streets or in homes, as Russians forbid residents from burying them," Sybiha wrote. "Families are starving, surviving on leftover garden vegetables, preserves and even snails ... Ukraine has repeatedly called for safe evacuation and international humanitarian access. These appeals cannot remain unanswered." The Kremlin acknowledged in September that Oleshky had [USN:R4N45100U TEXT:"critical problems"] with food and medical supplies but said Russia's military was working to resolve them. Ukraine's military has twice used drones to [USN:L1N45Q03T TEXT:"deliver food"] and medicine to the town. Sybiha urged the United Nations, the International Committee of the Red Cross and other organisations to "secure safe evacuation corridors and immediate humanitarian access." Oleshky lies on the east side of the Dnipro River in Kherson region, which Russian forces mostly occupied soon after the 2022 invasion. A Ukrainian counteroffensive later recaptured large chunks of territory, including the city of Kherson. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy described the situation in Oleshky this week as [USN:L8N45Y0E8 TEXT:""genocide.""] Oleshky had a pre-war population of 24,000 people and is now home to around 1,700 residents, including 47 children, according to Danielle Bell, head of the United Nations Human Rights Monitoring Mission in Ukraine. Local prosecutors said on Saturday Russian forces dropped aerial bombs on the city of Kherson, on the opposite bank of the Dnipro from Oleshky, killing an ambulance driver and wounding 40 people.

item.title: Muere en ataque a balazos reconocido exfiscal anticorrupción de Guatemala, crimen causa indignación
item.description: El abogado guatemalteco Juan Francisco Solórzano Foppa, reconocido por su lucha contra la corrupción en el país centroamericano, falleció tras ser atacado el sábado a balazos por dos dos hombres cuando dirigía a un equipo de fútbol durante un partido en un centro deportivo en la capital de Guatemala, en un crimen que causó indignación y fue condenado por defensores de derechos humanos y el presidente Bernardo Arévalo.
item.dc:creator: Sofia Menchu
item.content:encoded: El abogado guatemalteco Juan Francisco Solórzano Foppa, reconocido por su lucha contra la corrupción en el país centroamericano, falleció tras ser atacado el sábado a balazos por dos dos hombres cuando dirigía a un equipo de fútbol durante un partido en un centro deportivo en la capital de Guatemala, en un crimen que causó indignación y fue condenado por defensores de derechos humanos y el presidente Bernardo Arévalo. El ministro de Gobernación de Guatemala, Marco Antonio Villeda, dijo que una de las dos personas detenidas poco después del homicidio y que presuntamente habrían participado en el ataque era un exmilitar que había solicitado su baja del Ejército en febrero del 2019. En total, dijo el funcionario, se presume la participación de cuatro personas en el crimen. Los dos atacantes se acercaron a Solórzano Foppa cuando el abogado se alejó de sus escoltas y su hijo para moverse en el campo mientras dirigía al equipo de fútbol, dijo Villeda, quien no aventuró un móvil del sobre el homicidio. "Todavía no estamos en una etapa de certezas; estamos en una etapa de recolección de evidencias, análisis de indicios para construir una investigación sólida", dijo. "No vamos a adelantar en este momento conclusiones, ni tampoco vamos a excluir ninguna hipótesis ya que la verdad debe prevalecer y establecerse con pruebas", subrayó. El abogado, de 43 años, quien denunció la corrupción de empresarios y políticos, formó parte por poco tiempo en 2023 de la defensa del periodista guatemalteco [USN:L1N3Z81J8 TEXT:"José Rubén Zamora"], actualmente en arresto domiciliario, pero tuvo que dejar el caso tras ser acusado por el Ministerio Público de Consuelo Porras de obstaculizar el proceso y destruir u ocultar información. La policía había informado que había incautado un arma de fuego tipo carabina y una motocicleta al momento de detener a los dos presuntos atacantes. El homicidio causó revuelo en Guatemala y pedidos de justicia. La relatora especial de la ONU sobre la independencia de jueces y abogados, Margaret Satterthwaite, demandó en su cuenta de X el esclarecimiento de lo sucedido y que se "protejan a las autoridades de justicia del país". La embajada de Estados Unidos en Guatemala calificó en su cuenta de X de "atroz" lo sucedido y añadió que esperaba una investigación "completa y transparente que permita esclarecer los hechos". Solórzano Foppa se destacó por su lucha contra la corrupción cuando fue jefe de la Dirección de Investigaciones Criminalísticas en el Ministerio Público, así como cuando fungió entre 2016 y 2018 como jefe de la autoridad tributaria, SAT, cuando llevó a prisión y obligó a decenas de poderosos empresarios guatemaltecos a pagar impuestos. En 2025, Solórzano Foppa denunció una presunta vinculación entre la pandilla del Barrio 18 y el partido Unidad Nacional de la Esperanza (UNE) así como la existencia de vínculos entre las pandillas y el sistema judicial. Villeda dijo que la seguridad que recibía el exfiscal por parte del Estado desde 2010 se había incrementado en 2025 debido a su perfil político, pero no dio detalles, aunque aseguró que el abogado no había denunciado recientemente amenazas.

item.title: Chelsea's Martinez undergoes surgery after collision at Everton
item.description: Emi Martinez has undergone surgery following his collision with Everton's Jarrad Branthwaite, the Chelsea goalkeeper said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Emi Martinez has undergone surgery following his collision with Everton's Jarrad Branthwaite, the Chelsea goalkeeper said on Sunday, after his club's [USN:L1N463054 TEXT:"2-0 Premier League victory."] Pedro Neto's double on Saturday at the Hill Dickinson Stadium ended Everton's unbeaten start to the league season, but Chelsea's victory was overshadowed by the lengthy injury stoppage in the second half. Martinez and Branthwaite came together when Everton's Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall whipped a free kick into the box and, although the defender was back on his feet after treatment, the Argentina goalkeeper required treatment from paramedics. The 34-year-old was eventually strapped to a stretcher and carried off the field before being taken to hospital with a concussion, as Argentine media reported he had suffered a jaw injury in the collision. Martinez, wearing a hospital gown, posted on social media early on Sunday: "Thanks to everyone for the messages. The operation went well. "The most important thing is that we won, and kept a clean sheet. In a few weeks we'll be back." Martinez's injury forced Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso to give Mike Penders his Premier League debut, and the 21-year-old keeper helped Chelsea keep their first clean sheet in the league since January. Penders, a Belgian youth international, will likely have to step in until Martinez is cleared to return to training. Chelsea host Tottenham Hotspur in the league next Saturday followed by a League Cup fourth-round game at Liverpool on October 28 and a home Premier League match against Manchester United three days later. "Mike has personality. He's brave and we have full trust with him. He did well," Alonso told reporters. "He played in the cup games and whenever he's needed, like the other players whenever they are needed they can perform. "It's all about the squad, that all the players feel important and can have their moment whenever they are needed, and that's very positive."

item.title: Festival crush in Indian city of Kolkata kills at least 17, local media say
item.description: A crush at a religious festival in the eastern Indian city of Kolkata killed at least 17 people and injured dozens, local media reported on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A crush at a religious festival in the eastern Indian city of Kolkata killed at least 17 people and injured dozens, local media reported on Saturday. Durga Puja, a multi-day annual Hindu festival in the state of West Bengal, draws huge crowds to temporary structures known as pandals that house idols of the goddess Durga. The incident occurred at the exit gate in Kolkata's Girish Park area after heavy rain led to overcrowding as large numbers of devotees attempted to leave the venue, local TV said. Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi's office, in a post on social media platform X, announced a compensation payment of 200,000 rupees ($2,106.15) for the next of kin of those who died and 50,000 rupees each for the injured. ($1 = 94.9600 Indian rupees)

item.title: Israeli settlers attack Palestinians, European diplomats in West Bank, Belgium says
item.description: French and Polish diplomats and Catholic representatives were among those attacked, Belgium's foreign minister said, a day after settlers beat a Washington Post photojournalist.
item.dc:creator: Ali Sawafta, Mohammed Torokman
item.content:encoded: Israeli settlers attacked Palestinian civilians, European diplomats and a French mayor in the occupied West Bank on Saturday, Belgium's foreign minister said, a day after settlers beat an [USN:L8N4620II TEXT:"American photojournalist"]. Maxime Prevot said Belgium's consul general to the Palestinians, French and Polish diplomats, and Catholic representatives were among those attacked. A Belgian vehicle was also damaged, he said. "As the occupying power, Israeli authorities must protect Palestinians, ensure the safety of diplomats and journalists, and bring those responsible to justice. Impunity for violent settlers must end," Prevot said in a statement posted on X. 'THROWN TO THE GROUND' Bernard Baudoux, mayor of Aulnoye-Aymeries in northern France, told Reuters he had been harvesting olives near the Palestinian Christian village of Taybeh in solidarity with the local community when he was "violently attacked" by masked settlers. "I was thrown to the ground," he said. Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar condemned the attack, describing the perpetrators as Israeli rioters. He also suggested the diplomats should have coordinated their visit with the Israeli military. "Such coordination could have helped safeguard the visitors’ security," he said in a statement on X. Palestinian Vice President Hussein al-Sheikh condemned the attack, calling it a small example of the "daily terrorism" to which Palestinians are subjected. Israeli officials, including Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, have periodically condemned settler violence, while saying it is carried out by a small minority. Palestinians and human rights groups dispute that characterisation. ISRAELI POLICE OPEN INVESTIGATION Settler attacks on Palestinians in the West Bank have surged over the past three years. Journalists, activists and foreign observers have also been targeted. On Friday, dozens of masked settlers attacked Palestinians harvesting olives in the West Bank. Washington Post photojournalist Heidi Levine, a US citizen covering the harvest, was hospitalised after being assaulted by masked settlers. "Palestinians face this violence every day. Settlers also target journalists reporting on it and diplomats. Harvesting olives, reporting the news or carrying out diplomatic duties should never put anyone at risk of attack," Prevot said. Belgium, which has announced a ban on imports from Israeli settlements in the West Bank and the Golan Heights, will press for European Union sanctions "against those responsible for this violence and those who support them," he added. Polish Foreign Ministry spokesperson Maciej Wewior said on X that a convoy carrying diplomats, including Polish officials, had been attacked. The Polish diplomats were unharmed. "Attacks on members of the diplomatic corps are absolutely unacceptable," he said. Israeli police said they had opened an investigation into the incident. There was no immediate announcement of any arrests. Prosecutions of settlers accused of violent crimes against Palestinians in the West Bank are rare.

item.title: Huracán Trudy se fortalece aún más frente a costas del Pacífico mexicano
item.description: El huracán Trudy se fortaleció más la tarde del sábado en aguas del Pacífico mexicano y se espera aún un incremento en su fuerza en las próximas horas y que comience a debilitarse el domingo por la noche, mientras avanza hacia el noroeste acercándose a la costa, afectada por lluvias e inundaciones en las últimas semanas.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El huracán Trudy se fortaleció más la tarde del sábado en aguas del Pacífico mexicano y se espera aún un incremento en su fuerza en las próximas horas y que comience a debilitarse el domingo por la noche, mientras avanza hacia el noroeste acercándose a la costa, afectada por lluvias e inundaciones en las últimas semanas. Trudy se ubicaba a 180 kilómetros al sur-suroeste de Manzanillo, en el estado Colima. Sus vientos máximos sostenidos aumentaron a 155 kilómetros por hora (km/h), mientras su velocidad se mantenía a 17 km/h, de acuerdo al reporte más reciente del Centro Nacional de Huracanes de Estados Unidos (NHC, por su sigla en inglés). El aviso de huracán estaba vigente para la costa desde el sur de Manzanillo hasta Cabo Corrientes, Jalisco, en el occidente de México. "En la trayectoria del pronóstico, el centro de Trudy se acercará a la costa del suroeste y centro oeste de México esta tarde y pasará cerca de la costa esta noche y el domingo", dijo el NHC. Se espera que Trudy descargue lluvias de entre 10 a 20 centímetros a lo largo y cerca de la costa de Michoacán, Colima y Jalisco. "Esta lluvia puede producir inundaciones y deslizamientos de tierra que amenazan la vida, especialmente a lo largo de un terreno empinado", señala el informe del NHC. La estatal Comisión Nacional del Agua (Conagua) en México advirtió también que las precipitaciones generadas por Trudy, al que clasifica ahora como huracán categoría 2 en la escala Saffir-Simpson, podrían provocar desbordamientos e inundaciones en zonas bajas en las zonas involucradas. En las últimas semanas, la costa del Pacífico mexicano ha sido golpeada por los huracanes[USN:L6N45L0YK TEXT:" Polo"] y[USN:L8N45V0SM TEXT:" Simon,"] y la tormenta Rachel. Debido a las inundaciones, al menos ocho personas perdieron la vida en la ciudad costera de Ensenada, en el estado Baja California.

item.title: Hurricane Trudy gains strength near Mexico's coast, but is expected to weaken by Sunday
item.description: Hurricane Trudy gained some strength as it moved toward Mexico's western coast on Saturday, with forecasters warning it could strengthen a little more overnight before beginning to weaken on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Hurricane Trudy gained some strength as it moved toward Mexico's western coast on Saturday, with forecasters warning it could strengthen a little more overnight before beginning to weaken on Sunday. The US National Hurricane Center said Trudy was about 115 miles (180 km) south-southwest of Manzanillo on Saturday afternoon, with maximum sustained winds of 100 mph (155 kph). The hurricane was moving at about 10 mph (17 kph) and was forecast to approach the southwestern and west-central Mexican coast and pass near the coast overnight into Sunday. Hurricane conditions are expected in the warning area on Saturday night, while tropical storm conditions are expected to spread across the region on Saturday afternoon and evening, the NHC said. Hurricane conditions are also possible in areas under a hurricane watch. Trudy is forecast to bring 4 to 8 inches (10 to 20 cm) of rain, with higher totals of around 12 inches, across parts of Michoacan, Colima and Jalisco through the weekend, raising the risk of life-threatening flooding and landslides, especially in steep terrain, according to the NHC. Outer rain bands could produce 2 to 4 inches of rain, with isolated totals of around 6 inches, in Guerrero and Nayarit, where localized flash flooding is possible, the center said. The NHC also warned of dangerous storm surge accompanied by damaging waves in areas exposed to onshore winds. Swells generated by Trudy were already affecting parts of Mexico's southwestern coast and are expected to spread northward toward the country's west-central coast through the weekend, creating life-threatening surf and rip current conditions, the NHC said. Mexico's national water agency, CONAGUA, has officially classified Trudy as a Category 2 hurricane.
